topics.topic: Whether output file digests are supplied in payload fields or computed from returned content bytes
questions: Must the behavior specify computing each file digest from the returned content bytes, or must FilePayload and FileListPayload provide content_digest values?
Must FilePayload gain a content_digest field, or must the behavior specify computing the digest from FilePayload.content?
Must FileListPayload expose content digests, or must the behavior specify computing each digest from the corresponding bytes in contents?
Must FilePayload gain a content_digest field, or must the behavior require computing the file digest from its content bytes?
Must FileListPayload expose content digests for its files, or must the behavior require computing each digest from the corresponding content bytes?

quotes: - execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one — a value output's digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding its canonical bytes and a file output's is its content_digest, both computed from what the sandbox returned, and an expected output's is read from its stored record; the outcome is decided before any output is written, so no output is read back from the store —, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.
- FilePayload fields (exact, no others exist): content: bytes, payload_kind: Literal['file'], port: str
- FileListPayload fields (exact, no others exist): contents: tuple[bytes, ...], payload_kind: Literal['file_list'], port: str
judgement.why: The behavior requires a content_digest from returned file payloads, while the exact payload models have only content bytes and expressly permit no other fields.

topics.topic: Whether JSON-text bounds are measured on received UTF-8 text or canonical bytes
questions: Must each JSON-text bound be measured from its UTF-8 text as received before canonicalization, or from the canonical bytes returned by canonical_bytes?
Must each JSON-text bound be measured using canonical_bytes, or must it be measured on the received text before canonical_bytes is applied?

Must a JSON-text bound be measured from its UTF-8 bytes as received, allowing a larger canonical form, or from canonical_bytes, which measures the canonical form and can reject it before the stated final canonical-replacement step?

quotes: Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).

After every request bound is checked on the texts as received, as the last step of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1). A text whose canonical form outgrows a bound it met as received is not refused here: the module that judges the value measures its canonical bytes, as start_run refuses a run input whose canonical bytes exceed the stored value ceiling.
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires request bounds to be measured on the UTF-8 bytes as received before canonicalization and explicitly permits the canonical form to outgrow such a bound.
